content.text:
Confirmed. After commit `1e8d8cde5`, `onModification` calls `validatePath` unconditionally (the `validatePathUniqueness` guard was removed from inside `validatePath` and moved only into the new `onCreation`/`validateAndRenameFileOnce` path). This means renaming files/folders always enforced path uniqueness regardless of the `application.filesystem.unique.paths` config switch — exactly the bug that `bbcc596ff` fixes by re-adding the guard to `onModification`.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 1e8d8cde5bfab25b1d6e5ff39221c237374957f7

## Reasoning
(1) I traced the history of `AbstractFile.java` with `git log -p --follow`, searching for `validatePathUniqueness` and `onModification`, since the fix commit reintroduces a check on that exact field inside `onModification`.

(2) Commit `1e8d8cde5` ("The auto-renaming of newly created files/folders now happens onCreation...") refactored `validatePath`: previously the `if (validatePathUniqueness) { ... }` guard lived *inside* `validatePath`, protecting all callers. This commit removed that guard from `validatePath` (making it always check uniqueness) and instead added a `validatePathUniqueness` check only around the new `onCreation`/`validateAndRenameFileOnce` logic. It left `onModification` unchanged, still calling `validatePath(...)` directly, with no guard — so after this commit, renaming a file/folder always enforced path uniqueness, ignoring the `application.filesystem.unique.paths` config switch.

(3) The fix commit `bbcc596ff` adds back exactly the missing guard to `onModification`:
```java
boolean valid = true;
if (validatePathUniqueness) {
    valid = validatePath(securityContext, errorBuffer);
}
```
This mirrors the guard that existed inside `validatePath` before `1e8d8cde5` removed it, and matches the guard `1e8d8cde5` added to `onCreation` but forgot to add to `onModification`. This is a direct, high-confidence match — the intervening commits (`cf639bc72`, `19e8ada51`, `08f70aeab`, `5c4ca95e6`) don't touch this logic per the earlier `grep` output.
